transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-12-07
- Start: 14:00 UTC
- Duration: ~55 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonas (Redwood SE), Priya (CSM), Dr. Elena Ruiz (CTO), Marcus Lee (Head of Security), Sophie (PM), Aaron (Infra)
- Agenda: security posture intake for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private; KMS/BYOK, SSO/SAML, RBAC model, audit logs & retention

Summary:
Customer is evaluating Redwood for clinical note generation and de-identification pipelines. Primary concerns: bring-your-own-key (BYOK) and HSM support, SAML/SCIM integration with Okta, fine-grained RBAC and audit log exports into their Splunk stack, plus data residency and retention policies driven by healthcare regs. They are leaning towards Dedicated or Private because of regulatory constraints but want to understand tradeoffs and cost delta versus hosted with strict controls.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining. Quick intros, I'll hand it over to Jonas for the technical questions after a short context.
[00:12] Dr. Elena Ruiz: Hi all, thanks. I'm Elena, CTO. We're looking to deploy Redwood for our clinical summarization flows. Security is our top blocker so wanted to run through KMS, SSO, logs, retention stuff.
[00:20] Marcus Lee: Marcus, Head of Security. TL;DR we need to know if we can hold keys, rotate them, and get immutable audit trails.
[00:30] Maya: Absolutely. Jonas, do you want to kick off with encryption and KMS?
[00:33] Jonas (Redwood SE): Yeah sure, thanks. So high-level we support encryption in transit and at rest by default. For key management we offer customer-managed keys via cloud KMS for Hosted, and HSM-backed BYOK for Dedicated and Private. You can do AWS KMS CMKs, Azure Key Vault, or bring an HSM — we can integrate with CloudHSM or on-prem H S M appliances.
[01:01] Aaron Holt: Quick clarifying question — when you say BYOK for Hosted, is the key material ever in Redwood-managed HSMs or is it always in our KMS?
[01:10] Jonas: For Hosted BYOK we support envelope encryption where your KMS holds the master key and Redwood never has the plaintext master. For Hosted we typically set up key wrapping with your cloud KMS; Redwood holds wrapped keys transiently in memory during node startup. For Dedicated/Private, you can opt for direct HSM attachment or local KMS so keys never leave your control.
[01:28] Marcus: Is there dual-control or separation of duties? We need role separation for key management ops.
[01:34] Jonas: Yes, we support role-based access with optional dual-control workflows — you can require two admins to approve key rotations. Implementation depends a bit on your KMS/HSM capabilities; for example AWS CloudHSM + CloudKMS supports separation and access policies.
[01:46] Dr. Elena: Do you support periodic rotation and automatic rewrap? Our compliance team wants a 90-day rotation policy.
[01:51] Jonas: Yes, rotations can be automated via your KMS. We can also script a rotation runbook and integrate into your automation pipeline so the model runtime rewraps caches. Caveat: large KV cache entries may require coordinated warmup after rotation — we have hooks for that.
[02:06] Sophie Chen (PM): Sorry, what was KV cash?
[02:08] Jonas: Sorry, KV cache — the key/value attention cache in the runtime, yeah apologies the transcription picked it up odd.
[02:14] [laughter]
[02:18] Maya: Okay SSO/SAML — Marcus, you mentioned Okta in the pre-meeting notes?
[02:21] Marcus: Yes, we use Okta for SSO and want SCIM provisioning for groups and an audit trail of admin actions. Also SAML 2.0 assertions must include group claims.
[02:31] Jonas: We support SAML 2.0 and SCIM for user/provisioning. For Hosted we integrate with your IdP — SAML assertions and OIDC both supported. We persist login events and admin actions in the audit log and can stream logs to your SIEM.
[02:44] Aaron: Is SCIM provisioning available for Dedicated and Private as well?
[02:47] Jonas: Yes. In Dedicated it's typically configured inside the private control plane; in Private/on-prem you run the control plane in your VPC and configure SCIM endpoints to talk to your Okta instance over private networking.
[02:58] Marcus: How granular is RBAC? We need to map our SOC teams, infra, and product roles.
[03:04] Jonas: We support RBAC with built-in roles and custom role creation. You can grant per-model, per-route, and per-resource permissions. We also have token-scoped roles for programmatic access.
[03:14] Marcus: Do audit logs include token-level context, who called what model, and prompt hashes?
[03:20] Jonas: Logs include metadata: caller identity, route/model name, token usage, latencies, and request/response hashes for traceability. We can optionally redact full prompt text for privacy, but include hashes and truncated prompts for quality auditing.
[03:33] Dr. Elena: Where do logs live? Can they be pushed to our Splunk or S3 with encryption?
[03:38] Jonas: Yes, we can stream audit logs to your S3 buckets (server-side encryption with your KMS) or push to Splunk via HTTP Event Collector or syslog. For Dedicated/Private you can choose local retention and forced egress to your logging endpoints.
[03:51] Sophie: For data residency — we have PHI and must ensure data never leaves EU. What are your region guarantees?
[03:58] Maya: We have hosted regions in EU-West and can restrict routing to region-only; Dedicated and Private give you more control — Private can be deployed on-prem or in your VPC in the EU region.
[04:09] Marcus: Are you SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified? We need evidence for procurement.
[04:13] Maya: Yes, we are SOC 2 Type II; we also maintain ISO 27001 controls. I'll share the artifacts after the call.
[04:19] Marcus: Do you allow customers to run or commission independent pen tests for Dedicated/Private?
[04:24] Jonas: For Dedicated and Private, yes. For hosted we have a controlled process and allow third-party tests under NDA; there are limited windows for hosted tests to avoid impacting other customers.
[04:35] Aaron: Network connectivity — if we go Dedicated, can we VPC peering or set up private link?
[04:39] Jonas: We support VPC peering, PrivateLink, and VPN tunnels depending on cloud. For on-prem Private we do an air-gapped option and a private control plane pattern.
[04:48] Dr. Elena: What about data retention — our legal requires 7 years for some logs, but we don't want full prompts stored for that long. Can we configure different retention windows per artifact?
[04:58] Jonas: Yes. Retention is configurable per artifact: raw prompts, de-identified outputs, and audit logs can each have independent retention. For Hosted we have retention tiers; for Dedicated/Private you can set retention policies and automatic purge. We also support legal hold flags.
[05:12] Marcus: Can you redact PHI automatically before logs hit storage?
[05:16] Jonas: We offer optional pre-ingestion de-identification pipelines that can mask or tokenise PHI. However, for some compliance scenarios we keep hashes to allow deduping without storing PII.
[05:28] Sophie: Regarding cost trade-offs — if we require HSM-backed keys plus long retention and log streaming to Splunk, is that leaning us toward Dedicated?
[05:36] Maya: Practically yes. Hosted can meet many controls but Dedicated gives you fixed capacity, private networking and isolates the key material more cleanly — it's usually where customers with strict data residency/retention rules land.
[05:45] Dr. Elena: We also have to provide auditors with immutable audit trails. Do you support WORM-style logs or append-only storage?
[05:51] Jonas: We support append-only write patterns and can export to WORM-compliant storage like S3 Object Lock for audit evidence.
[05:58] Marcus: On disaster recovery — if we lose a node, how do you guarantee keys and logs remain available?
[06:03] Jonas: For redundancy we replicate encrypted blobs across availability zones and the KMS provider handles regional redundancy. For Private we recommend a multi-AZ deployment and have runbooks for failover.
[06:14] [pause / typing sounds]
[06:18] Aaron: A bit of an oddball question — do you support hardware attestation on the compute nodes?
[06:22] Jonas: We have optional attestation via Nitro Enclaves / TPM attest for certain cloud and on-prem configs; it's advanced but available for customers with high-assurance needs.
[06:30] Dr. Elena: Great. Can we map what evidence you will give to our control framework? We use a mapper for their internal auditor — traceability matrix mapping to SOC2 controls.
[06:39] Maya: We'll produce a controls mapping doc showing how Redwood controls map to SOC2/ISO controls and evidence locations. I'll own that deliverable.
[06:46] Marcus: Do you log admin console actions? We need to see who created keys, rotated, who changed roles.
[06:52] Jonas: Yes admin console events are tracked, including API tokens, role changes, and key operations. These can be forwarded to your SIEM.
[06:59] Sophie: Are there any constraints around model checkpoint storage? For some models we want to ensure model artifacts aren't stored in multi-tenant buckets.
[07:06] Jonas: Model artifacts for Hosted are in our managed stores, but we offer model pinning and private model hosting in Dedicated/Private so artifacts reside in your tenancy.
[07:14] Marcus: How do you handle subpoena/requests — is there an access governance policy?
[07:19] Maya: Redwood responds according to our legal process; for Dedicated/Private you control data and are the data controller — so you handle legal requests directly; for Hosted we assist but do have process. We'll share the legal notes doc.
[07:30] [crosstalk briefly]
[07:34] Aaron: For proof-of-concept — can we get a 4-week Dedicated pilot to run benchmarks and log exports?
[07:39] Maya: We typically run a 30-day pilot for Dedicated with a reduced commitment; we'll include sizing and a cost delta. Jonas will scope technical reqs.
[07:46] Jonas: For the pilot we'll need network info, expected QPS and typical sequence length distribution to size GPUs and KV cache. Also sample prompt sets for quality tests — scrubbed/de-identified samples are fine.
[07:59] Dr. Elena: On the scrubbed samples — we need to ensure de-id before sharing. Marcus will handle that.
[08:05] Marcus: Yep. We'll provide synthetic or de-identified data.
[08:09] Maya: Anything else re compliance?
[08:11] Marcus: One last: can Redwood support customer-side encryption of audit logs such that Redwood cannot decrypt them even for debugging?
[08:18] Jonas: Yes, you can configure audit logs to be encrypted with your KMS keys and Redwood won't have the decryption rights; we rely on your SIEM to show decrypted events. There is tradeoff on troubleshooting — we'll need a process for redaction/gated access.
[08:32] Dr. Elena: Good. That covers most. Quick cost question — is there a published delta percent we can reference between Hosted with BYOK and Dedicated?
[08:40] Maya: It's use-case dependent but ballpark Dedicated is 2.5x-4x Hosted for reserved GPU capacity and operational overhead; we'll put a more accurate estimate in the follow-up.
[08:51] Sophie: Can you include an itemized list of what adds to the cost (HSM, log egress, long retention)?
[08:56] Maya: Yes we'll include that in the pricing appendix.
[09:01] [silence, typing]
[09:08] Maya: Okay time for wrap — recap and next steps. Jonas, want to summarize technical open items?
[09:12] Jonas: Sure: 1) Provide VPC/private link diagram and Dedicated sizing options; 2) Share sample audit log schema and Splunk export examples; 3) Prepare retention mapping templates; 4) Document BYOK/HSM integration steps.
[09:26] Maya: And from the AE side: I'll send SOC2/ISO and pen test artifacts; propose pilot timeline and pricing; set up infra deep dive for next week.
[09:35] Dr. Elena: Sounds good. Marcus will send de-identified sample prompts. Aaron will share network contact.
[09:42] Sophie: We'll also do a procurement timeline — we need vendor evidence by end of year.
[09:47] Maya: Great. We'll follow up with a calendar invite for the deep dive and attach artifacts. Thanks everyone.
[09:52] [meeting ends]

Notes on transcription: occasional ASR errors: "K V cache" instead of KV cache, "Samuel" for SAML in one snippet (not present above), some punctuation oddities. Originals/prompt samples were requested; actual PII will be sanitized before upload.
